2027-06-03.title: Saints Charles Lwanga and Companions, Martyrs
readings: Grant that she and I may find mercy and that we may grow old together
Happy is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways
You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart … You shall love your neighbor as yourself
2027-06-03.alt: Memorial. Thursday of the Ninth Week in Ordinary Time (Year I). The weekday readings are given here (first reading in NRSV numbering); the proper readings of the memorial, 2 Maccabees 7:1–2, 9–14 (the seven brothers) and Matthew 5:1–12a (the Beatitudes), may be used instead. St Charles Lwanga and twenty-one companions, the Catholic martyrs of Uganda, died between 1885 and 1887, most of them burned at Namugongo on 3 June 1886. Liturgical colour: red.
2027-06-03.verse: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.
theo: The Book of Tobit now reaches its love story. Young Tobias has set out on a long journey for his blind father, with a companion who calls himself Azariah but is really the angel Raphael. As they approach Ecbatana, Raphael tells him about Sarah, the daughter of their kinsman Raguel: “the girl is sensible, brave, and very beautiful, and her father is a good man.” Tobias is afraid, and with reason: seven husbands have died on their wedding night. But Raphael says: “Do not be afraid, for she was set apart for you before the world was made.” At Raguel's house there are tears of recognition and a warm welcome. Raguel is honest about the danger, yet he gives his daughter in marriage with a blessing: “May the Lord of heaven, my child, guide and prosper you both this night and grant you mercy and peace.” A marriage contract is written. Then comes the wedding night. Before anything else, Tobias rises and says to Sarah: “Sister, get up, and let us pray and implore our Lord that he grant us mercy and safety.” Their prayer is one of the most beautiful in the Bible on marriage. It begins with praise: “Blessed are you, O God of our ancestors, and blessed is your name in all generations forever.” It remembers creation: “You made Adam, and for him you made his wife Eve as a helper and support.” And it offers an honest heart: “I now am taking this kinswoman of mine, not because of lust, but with sincerity. Grant that she and I may find mercy and that we may grow old together.” And together they say: “Amen, Amen.” A marriage that begins on its knees is protected from evil. The Psalm blesses such a home: “Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house; your children will be like olive shoots around your table.”

In the Gospel a scribe, impressed by Jesus' answers, asks a sincere question: “Which commandment is the first of all?” Jesus answers with the Shema, the prayer every devout Jew says morning and evening: “Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one; you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.” And he joins to it a second commandment from Leviticus 19:18: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” The scribe agrees warmly and adds that this love is “much more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” Jesus looks at him and says: “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” Here a Jewish teacher and Jesus stand together on the foundation of Israel's faith, the love of the one God and of neighbour. Tobias and Sarah lived this double love on their wedding night: love of God first, in prayer, and then a love for each other that is sincere and pure. The martyrs of Uganda lived it to the point of fire. Charles Lwanga, head of the royal pages at the court of Kabaka Mwanga II, protected the boys in his care from the king's sinful demands and taught them the faith. When the persecution broke out, he baptised several catechumens the night before their arrest. On 3 June 1886, at Namugongo, he and many companions were burned alive, praying for their persecutors. Charles is said to have told the executioner that it was as if he were pouring water on him. Some of the pages were barely fourteen. With them died Anglican Christians too, witnesses to the same Lord. St Paul VI canonised the twenty-two Catholic martyrs in 1964, and today the Church of Africa, rich in faith, is their harvest.

live: If you are married, pray one short prayer with your spouse tonight; if you are not, pray tonight for one married couple you know.
Choose one area, heart, soul, mind or strength, that you give God least, and offer it to him today.
saints: The Missionaries of Africa (White Fathers) reached the Kingdom of Buganda in 1879, and the faith spread quickly among young men at the royal court. Kabaka Mwanga II turned against the Christians, angered by their refusal of his immoral demands and by their loyalty to Christ above the king. Joseph Mukasa Balikuddembe, who had rebuked the king, was beheaded on 15 November 1885. Charles Lwanga, who succeeded him as head of the royal pages, protected the boys and instructed them; on the night before their arrest in May 1886 he baptised several of them. On 3 June 1886 (Ascension Day) Charles and many others were burned alive at Namugongo. Twenty-two Catholic martyrs, the youngest, Kizito, about fourteen, were beatified in 1920 and canonised by St Paul VI on 18 October 1964. Anglican Christians also died in the same persecution. Namugongo is today a great place of pilgrimage on 3 June.
2027-06-03.prayer: O God, who have made the blood of martyrs the seed of Christians, mercifully grant that the field which is your Church, watered by the blood shed by Saints Charles Lwanga and his companions, may be fertile and always yield you an abundant harvest. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Lord, bless all married couples with the prayer of Tobias and Sarah, give our young people pure and brave hearts, and teach us to love you with all our heart and our neighbour as ourselves. Amen.
altar: The scribe said that love of God and neighbour is worth more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices. At this altar we offer the one sacrifice that is pure love: Christ, who loved the Father with all his heart and loved us to the end. The martyrs of Uganda joined their lives to that offering. When we receive him, we receive the strength to love as he loved.

quick: Tobias marries Sarah, and on their wedding night they first pray together: Grant that she and I may find mercy and that we may grow old together.
Jesus names the first commandment, to love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength, and the second, to love your neighbour as yourself; a scribe is told he is not far from the kingdom.
St Charles Lwanga and his young companions in Uganda kept their faith and purity and were burned at Namugongo on 3 June 1886.
2027-06-03.action: Pray tonight for married couples, and offer God one part of yourself that you have held back.
2027-06-03.question: Do I love God with all my heart, soul, mind and strength, or only with what is left over?
kidsaint: Kizito was a boy in Uganda, only about fourteen, who served in the king's palace. He learned about Jesus from Charles Lwanga, the leader of the palace boys, and he wanted very much to be baptised. When the king began to kill Christians, Kizito was baptised by Charles the night before they were arrested. On the way to death he held Charles's hand and was not afraid. Lesson: even a young person can be very brave for Jesus, and a good friend helps you stay faithful.

family.explain: Tobias and Sarah got married. On their wedding night, before anything else, they knelt down together and prayed. They thanked God for making husband and wife, and they asked him to let them grow old together. Families that pray together are strong. Jesus also said that the greatest commandment is to love God with all our heart and to love our neighbour as ourselves.
family.intention: We pray for our parents and grandparents, for all married couples, and for young people who must be brave for Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When can our family pray together every day this week?”

illus: A couple in Kollam celebrating their fiftieth wedding anniversary were asked by their grandchildren what their secret was. The grandmother smiled and said that on their wedding night, before anything else, her husband had asked her to kneel with him and pray the Our Father. Then, she said, we did it again the next night, and the next, for fifty years. On the nights we were angry with each other, it was hard to start, but we never ended the day without it. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, our God, you are one Lord. We want to love you with all our heart, soul, mind and strength, and to love one another as ourselves. Be among us now. Amen.
share: Sister, get up, and let us pray (Tobit 8:4). How much does prayer shape my family life?
Not because of lust, but with sincerity (Tobit 8:7). How can I help the young people I know to love purely?
You are not far from the kingdom of God (Mark 12:34). What still keeps me from loving God with my whole self?
pm.resp: Happy is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways.
interc: For married couples, that like Tobias and Sarah they may begin and end each day in prayer.
For young men and women preparing for marriage, that they may love with sincerity and purity.
For the Church in Uganda and in all Africa, that the seed of the martyrs may bear abundant fruit.
For young people who are pressured to do wrong by those in power, that they may have the courage of the Uganda martyrs.
For Christians of every Church who suffer for Christ, and for unity among all who confess his name.
pm.close: Father, the martyrs of Uganda loved you more than life. Give us their courage and their purity, and keep our homes in your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today's first reading is a wedding story. Young Tobias comes to the house of his kinsman Raguel and asks to marry Sarah. Everyone knows the danger: seven husbands have died on their wedding night. But the angel Raphael has told Tobias: do not be afraid, she was set apart for you before the world was made. So Raguel gives his daughter with a blessing, and a marriage contract is written.

Then comes the wedding night, and what does Tobias do first? He says to Sarah: sister, get up, and let us pray (Tobit 8:4). Before anything else, the two of them stand before God. They praise him, they remember how he made man and woman, and Tobias says: I take her not because of lust, but with sincerity; grant that she and I may grow old together (Tobit 8:7). And Sarah answers: Amen. What a beautiful beginning for a marriage! Love that begins in prayer is protected from evil.

In the Gospel Jesus tells us that the first commandment is to love God with all our heart, soul, mind and strength, and the second is to love our neighbour as ourselves (Mark 12:30–31). Tobias and Sarah did exactly that. First God, then each other. Our families too need this order. When God is first, love between husband and wife, parents and children, is pure and strong.

Today we also remember St Charles Lwanga and his companions, young Christians in Uganda. The king demanded of the palace boys what was sinful, and Charles protected them. When they refused to give up their faith, they were burned alive at Namugongo in 1886. Some of them were only fourteen. They loved God with all their strength, more than their own lives. Let us ask them to give our young people pure and brave hearts, and let us ask Tobias and Sarah to teach our families to pray together. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know the most important rule in the whole world? Jesus told us: love God with all your heart, and love your neighbour as much as you love yourself. Long ago in Uganda some boys your age loved Jesus so much that they would not do something wrong even when the king ordered them. They were very brave. Today, show your love for God by saying a prayer, and your love for others by being kind.

intro: Theme: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart.”
A wedding night that begins in prayer, the first and second commandments, and young martyrs who loved God more than life.

You are not far from the kingdom of God.

concl: Tobias and Sarah show us love that puts God first and so loves the other purely; Jesus names that order as the heart of the Law.
The martyrs of Uganda loved God with all their strength and kept their purity to the point of death; their blood has become the seed of a great Church.
2027-06-03.resolve: Put God first each day this week: begin the morning with the Shema and end the evening with a prayer together with your family.
